first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that reducing onboarding friction improved completion, time-to-value, and durable early activation. This is more directly tied to sustainable qualified revenue than reacting to competitor pricing, which may carry downstream margin or customer-quality risk. Verification should confirm segment applicability, experiment design, and durability before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard guarded simplification experiment focused on self-serve SMB onboarding. Exp_86 directly supports the current completion decline, with completion +13%, faster time-to-value, and 30-day retention +3%. Exp_31 also showed SMB activation +9% and qualified revenue +4%, but its -1% retention result warrants explicit retention and customer-quality guardrails. The evidence is segment-specific, so this should not be a broad rollout.

final2.rationale: Pivot this cycle's experiment to targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMB accounts because the competitive threat has intensified and churn conversations have doubled. Memory_73 supports acquisition and revenue lift in this segment, but its source was not verified this cycle. Use a small, time-limited test with qualified-revenue, retention, discount-depth, and margin guardrails rather than a broad price cut. The onboarding evidence remains valid, but pricing is now the more urgent threat to sustainable revenue.
